factual_summaries.summary: A public context-engineering article frames repository context as a cost and quality bottleneck for coding agents, citing token-metered pricing pressure and local context layers that reduce repeated repo exploration. It specifically discusses context-router as a memory-aware MCP-native context engine that stores observations in git and returns a minimal useful slice to future agents.

TechRadar Pro argues that autonomous agents should be treated as first-class digital identities with discoverability, assigned human ownership, policies, auditability, and just-in-time privileged access rather than direct exposure to long-lived secrets.

Cycode summarizes the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 and maps agentic defenses to goal constraints, untrusted retrieved content, per-agent identity with short-lived credentials, AIBOM-backed supply-chain provenance, sandboxed execution, behavioral monitoring, and kill switches across IDE, CLI, and PR workflows.

The arXiv preprint proposes an Agent Governance Manifest for OSS collaboration, arguing that agent-mediated contributions need repository-hosted rules coordinating risk, evidence, accountability, preparation obligations, verification rights, and maintainer decision authority. In its study, AGM-supported materials improved reviewer risk-label recovery and perceived review support.

Gensee published a 15-question readiness checklist for deploying coding agents, requiring runtime evidence for isolation, authorization boundaries, file and secret access, prompt integrity, command safety, network egress, workflow visibility, long-horizon safety, provenance, runtime policy enforcement, rollback, recovery, human governance, explainability, and incident readiness.

Cursor changed its Slack integration so it shares a plan before starting, can start in a named multi-repo environment, prompts when it needs to switch repositories mid-task, and can read from or send status to other Slack channels and threads.
